decision.question: How does an end line get written when a server is killed with taskkill /F (no exit handler runs)?
options: sweep closes the ledger: a start line whose pid is gone gets an end line with why 'found gone'
decision.chose: both: a sync append in process.on('exit') for clean exits, and the sweep closes any start whose pid died
decision.why: taskkill /F and a closed console never run JS; only an outside check can see those deaths

decision.question: Who removes a landed task's worktree from disk?
options: the reaper stops only processes; worktree-sweep (already on the task-loop tick) removes the tree once merged
decision.why: worktree-down deletes the branch; a landed-but-unmerged branch would lose commits. worktree-sweep already checks merged

CAUGHT: pid reuse. qf-4's recorded watcher_pid 25792 is now whisper-server.exe. Pool.kill() used to taskkill /T any recorded pid blindly — it would have killed the owner's dictation. Pool.kill(pid, expect) now checks the command line first (worktree-logs/<id>.log for the server, health-supervisor for the watcher); the Lifecycle reaper checks a logged pid's birth time against its start line. During the real salvage the guard fired: 'pid 25792 is no longer ours (whisper-server) — not killed'.
